row.evidence: Snowflake supports SCIM 2.0, lets you integrate Snowflake with Okta and Microsoft Azure AD as identity providers. You can use custom identity providers.
row.notes: Status unchanged from June (free). Consumption-priced: no per-user price, so per-user fields and the multiplier are null (June's multiplier of 1 is dropped because both price sides are null). The per-credit dollar amounts on the pricing page load per platform/region via script and could not be quoted, so June's ~$2.00-2.50/credit figure is not carried forward. No edition restriction on SCIM: Snowflake marks edition-gated docs with an 'Enterprise Edition Feature' banner (for example Access History), and none of the SCIM pages carry one; SSO is ticked for every edition, Standard included, in the editions feature table (tier mapping read from the table's tick cells). Legacy SCIM access tokens expire after six months; External OAuth and programmatic access tokens are the current options. SCIM groups map one-to-one to Snowflake roles.

scim.base_url: https://<account_identifier>.snowflakecomputing.com/scim/v2/ (or /scim/v2/<integration_uuid>/ with External OAuth or programmatic access tokens)

auth.token_source: External OAuth token, programmatic access token for a SERVICE user, or legacy SCIM access token from SELECT SYSTEM$GENERATE_SCIM_ACCESS_TOKEN('<integration>')
auth.token_expiry: Legacy SCIM access token: six months; JWT and PAT lifetimes per their own settings

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivation sets the user's DISABLED property to TRUE; disabling aborts the user's running and scheduled queries and locks the user out. A SCIM DELETE drops the user; objects the user created (tables, views) are not dropped because they are owned by roles.

custom.how: allowedInterfaces, defaultWarehouse, defaultRole, defaultSecondaryRoles, type and snowflakeTags, sent in urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User (Okta) or urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:2.0:User (Entra and custom)

roles.how: SCIM groups are Snowflake roles (one-to-one); defaultRole and defaultSecondaryRoles custom attributes set the session defaults

rate_limits.text: Maximum of 500 concurrent requests per account per SCIM endpoint (/Users, /Groups); HTTP 429 beyond that.

limitations.text: Users and roles must be owned by the SCIM provisioner role (OKTA_PROVISIONER, AAD_PROVISIONER or GENERIC_SCIM_PROVISIONER) or IdP updates do not sync.
Changes made directly in Snowflake do not synchronise back to the IdP.
Only userName (Users) and displayName (Groups) can be filtered; only eq and sw; no compound filters.
Multi-value user attributes are not supported.
Okta Enhanced Group Push and Push Now are not supported; existing Snowflake roles cannot be brought under Okta management.
Group members list only users directly granted the role, not those who inherit it through the role hierarchy.
Private connectivity (privatelink) URLs cannot be used for the SCIM integration; the public endpoint and a network policy allowing the IdP's IPs are required.
SYNC_PASSWORD is supported only for Okta SCIM integrations.
Snowflake sends invitation emails to SCIM-created users by default; opting out requires Snowflake Support.

citations.title: Authenticating SCIM API requests
citations.quote: Snowflake authenticates SCIM API requests from identity providers through a Bearer token in the Authorization header of HTTP requests. Snowflake accepts different types of tokens in the header.

citations.title: Authenticating SCIM API requests
citations.quote: Snowflake provides a long-lived token that is unique to SCIM API requests. This token is valid for six months.

citations.title: SCIM user API reference
citations.quote: Create a user¶ Method and endpoint: POST /scim/v2/Users Description: Creates a user in Snowflake.

citations.title: SCIM group API reference
citations.quote: Create a group¶ Method and endpoint: POST /scim/v2/Groups Description: Creates a new group in Snowflake.

citations.title: SCIM API requests
citations.quote: Snowflake provides the following SCIM APIs: User API: Allows identity providers to do the following actions: Check whether users exist. Get details about users. List users. Create and activate users. Update user attributes. Deactivate users.

citations.title: SCIM user API reference
citations.quote: Method and endpoint: GET /scim/v2/Users/{{user_id}} Description: Returns details about a user associated with the user_id path parameter.

citations.title: SCIM user API reference
citations.quote: PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{{id}} Description: Replaces attributes of the user associated with the id path parameter. You must set op to replace to perform this HTTP request. active allows the following values: false: deactivates the user. true: activates the user.

citations.title: SCIM user API reference
citations.quote: PUT /scim/v2/Users/{{id}} Description: Updates the attributes of the user associated with the id path parameter.

citations.title: SCIM user API reference
citations.quote: DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{{id}} Description: Deletes the user associated with the id path parameter.

citations.title: SCIM group API reference
citations.quote: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{{group_id}} Description: Updates the display name attribute or group membership of the group associated with the group_id path parameter.
